title: Hypothesis (O): K_{x,0+}-vs-M_{x,0+} transversality on B(M)
body_html:
Hypothesis (O)

Hypothesis (O). For each vertex $x \in A \subseteq \mathcal{B}(M)$ and each $d \geq 0$: if $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{F}' \in \mathcal{B}(M)_d$ and $\mathcal{F}' = k \cdot \mathcal{F}$ for some $k \in K_{x, 0+}$, then there exists $m \in M_{x, 0+}$ with $\mathcal{F}' = m \cdot \mathcal{F}$.

(O) is a transversality hypothesis: the pro-$p$ part $K_{x, 0+}$ of $K_x$ does not bring $\mathcal{B}(M)$-cells to genuinely new $\mathcal{B}(M)$-cells beyond the $M_{x, 0+}$-action. Equivalently, $K_{x, 0+}$ admits a (set-theoretic) decomposition $K_{x, 0+} = M_{x, 0+} \cdot P_x$ in which $P_x \subseteq K_{x, 0+}$ does not stabilise any $\mathcal{B}(M)$-cell setwise.

Role: isolating mock-exp from the main framework

(O) is the substantive content of the orbit bijection ([[node:depth_zero_reduction.M_K_orbit_bijection]] Lemma): in the present formulation (option (B) of the 2026-05-25 audit), the abstract framework consumes (O) as a black box, and the mock-exponential machinery of $[$Adler, §1.5$]$ enters only at the verification of (O) in each application.

This is the cleanest separation: the cartesian-cosheaf framework of Cartesian cosheaves Cosh^cart_G(X,R,φ) and unit isomorphism does not see mock-exp anywhere; mock-exp is fully isolated to the application-specific verification step.

Why (O) cannot be eliminated entirely

Mock-exp's substantive content is precisely the existence of the transversal $P_x = \varphi(\mathfrak{k}^\perp_{x, 0+})$ inside $K_{x, 0+}$. This is a real structural fact about the relation between $K$ and $M$ that does not follow from any abstract axiom ((T1)–(T5), (K1)–(K4), (E1)–(E4)).

In comparison: - Lanard's framework (no $M$-vs-$G$ distinction): the question does not arise. - Dat–Fintzen (with $M$-vs-$G$): cites Adler explicitly.

So the dependency is real. (O) is the cleanest way to record it.

Verification in the two applications

Classical case

Mock-exp via the Cayley transform on $\mathfrak{gl}_F(V)$ [Stevens:SC App A], descended to $G^\beta$ via Galois; explicitly verifies (O) by producing the transversal $P_x = \varphi(\mathfrak{k}^\perp_{x, 0+})$ inside $K_{x, 0+}$.

Tame case

Mock-exp via the exponential map on the Lie algebra (large $p$), $\varphi_x = \exp$ on $\mathfrak{m}^\perp_{x, 0+}$; the corresponding transversal is verified across the apartment using parabolic Bruhat decomposition in the enveloping group, plus Galois descent [Adler, §1.5].

Abstract case

(O) is an additional axiom that must be verified case-by-case (parahoric, classical, tame all check, abstract is open).

See also

  • [[node:depth_zero_reduction.M_K_orbit_bijection]] — the orbit bijection that uses (O) as its substantive injectivity content.
  • [[node:depth_zero_reduction.K4_hypothesis]] — the reductive-quotient hypothesis (K4); (K4) gives the surjectivity part of the orbit bijection (via the Levi splitting $K_x = K_{x, 0+} \cdot M_x$), while (O) gives injectivity.
  • Good mock exponential map and factorization M × m^⊥_{x,0+} → MG_{x,0+} — the mock-exp construction that verifies (O) in classical / tame cases.

Open question

Can (O) be derived from a cartesian-cosheaf-style axiom (e.g., a categorical compatibility condition on the functor $[A/\mathscr K_M] \to [A/\mathscr K]$)? If so, mock-exp could be eliminated entirely from the framework. Currently open.
